featured_reviews.name: Anusha Sundaram
featured_reviews.review_text:
I've heard so much about the wonders of The Boston Cupcakery. However, our enthusiasm to try out this place wasn't translated into a wonderful experience.

This small outlet is located within a dense commercial/residential area. You'd need a cab to get here because parking was a little difficult.

There isn't a lot of seating. Only one table is there in the AC area and another in the outside seating area. There isn't any music available and the lighting was really off. The lights kept flickering. We had to request that they be switched off.

We first went in for the 24-layer Pastry. This is a very good dessert. Even though there are so many layers of cream and cake, the dessert wasn't very heavy. It's great for sharing.

The next came the Red Velvet Pastry. There's no other way to describe it than just plain terrible. This is the worst version of this cake I have had so far. The cake looked a little slumped when it was served to us but we didn't think much about it. With one small slice, the entire pastry collapsed. The cake itself wasn't so good and the icing was very off. There were instances where we thought this might be a cheesecake but it wasn't. The cake had a room temperature which might indicate that the refrigeration of the desserts aren't up to the mark.

I'm not pleased with the variation in the quality of desserts. One was good while the other was terrible making it difficult for me to recommend this place.

Extremely Disappointed with Dale’s Eden!

This was my third order from Dale’s Eden and my second from the app. I have always trusted Dale’s Eden for fresh, high-quality cakes, but this time was a complete disaster.

We ordered a mixed fruit cake, and what we received was completely stale and unfit for consumption. The guests who received it were appalled—it wasn’t even worth tasting, and there were genuine concerns that eating it could lead to health issues.

To make matters worse, the cake contained orange slices with their peel still on—a clear sign of poor preparation and quality control.

It was only later that we realized the cake was likely at least three days old, possibly leftover from before Eid. If that’s the case, it’s completely unacceptable and unethical to sell such an old product to customers.

This experience has shattered our trust in Dale’s Eden, and I will never order from them again. Selling stale cakes is not just bad service—it’s a serious health risk!

I celebrated my Golden Retriever Joey’s first birthday, and I ordered his cake from Doggy Bakery — and I must say, it was a wonderful experience. The cake was delivered on time, beautifully designed, and looked absolutely amazing.
The most important part for me was that Joey has a very sensitive stomach, yet he had no stomach upset at all after eating the cake. They were perfectly fine, active, and clearly loved the taste — their expressions said it all. Because they enjoyed the cake so naturally, it truly made Joey’s birthday even more special.

Overall, I absolutely loved the cake — it was beautiful, well-designed, and clearly pet-safe. This is a fantastic initiative, and I’m definitely looking forward to ordering many more things from Doggy Bakery in the future. Highly recommended! 🐶🎂💛

If you’re in the area, Deliure is totally worth popping into. Whether you're a dessert nerd or just in the mood for something good, this place hits the spot.

I am writing to express my deep disappointment and concern regarding a recent purchase from your bakery.  On May 18, 2024, I bought a box of cookies, Chocolate Walnut Biscuits along with two other snack packets Bakarwadi from your shop, believing them to be vegetarian based on the green mark on the packaging. After bringing the cookies home, we consumed them, assuming they were vegetarian. To confirm our suspicions, we called your shop and were informed that the cookies are, in fact, non-vegetarian. This revelation was extremely distressing for us. Being strict vegetarians, consuming non-vegetarian food is against our dietary beliefs and religious sentiments. This incident has caused us significant emotional distress and has deeply affected our faith in the integrity of your bakery. We request the following actions from your end to address this issue: A formal apology acknowledging the error and its impact on us. Assurance that such incidents will not occur in the future, including a review and correction of your labeling practices.
Compensation for the distress and inconvenience caused to us. Enclosed photographs of the cookie box with the scratched mark, as well as other items we purchased from your shop clearly labeled as 100% vegetarian. We trust you understand the gravity of this matter and expect a prompt and satisfactory resolution.
